questions.stem: A 47-year-old man presented with an intensely painful ulcer of 13 days’ duration over the glans penis, surrounding the urethral orifice. The lesion had started as multiple small superficial ulcers, which had then coalesced. The ulcer had distinct raised thickened erythematous edges. There was necrotic slough and a foul-smelling hemopurulent discharge. The penis was edematous, and there was bilateral tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. He had had unprotected insertive and receptive anal sex with at least 20 men in the preceding 3 months. Investigations: HIV: Ag/Ab negative Syphilis: EIA negative Direct wet mount microscopy: trophozoites containing ingested red blood cells
questions.lead_in: What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.explanation: Entamoeba histolytica Primary infection of the skin by Entamoeba histolytica can be acquired by direct contact with an infected subject during vaginal or anal intercourse. Identification of trophozoites containing ingested red blood cells is consistent with a clinical picture of amebic infection. Biopsy may be necessary to demonstrate trophozoites and to exclude other diagnoses such as squamous cell carcinoma. PCR may be useful in confirming the diagnosis. (Image from Assessments. In Cohen J, Powderly W , Opal S, eds. Infectious Diseases. 4th ed. Elsevier; 2017.)

questions.question: [image-based question: Staph streak on BAP shown with satelliting colonies]

parts.text: Name 3 genera of bacteria that have this characteristic.

questions.model_answer: Three genera exhibiting satellite phenomenon around a Staphylococcus streak on blood agar (due to Staph-produced NAD/hemin/X-V factors): (1) Haemophilus (e.g. H. influenzae, requires X and V factors). (2) Aggregatibacter (formerly Actinobacillus) actinomycetemcomitans. (3) Granulicatella / Abiotrophia (nutritionally variant streptococci, satellite due to pyridoxal requirement).

questions.question: 27. You isolate from both aerobic and anaerobic blood culture bottles a gram negative pathogen that grows well on sheep blood agar and chocolate agar, but fails to grow on MacConkey.

parts.text: List 2 organisms (from different genus) that meet all these characteristics.

cohort_answer.text: (fastidious Gram negs) Pasteurella multocida (gram- coccobacilli); Capnocytophaga canimorsus (gram- rod); Eikenella corrodens (gram- rod); Brucella; Bartonella; Francisella.

questions.question: AM 24. Name 5 of the most common gram negative organisms that cause IE (genus only) (2.5)

parts.text: Name 5 of the most common Gram negative organisms that cause IE

cohort_answer.text: Haemophilus spp.; Aggregatibacter spp. (Actinomycetemcomitans); Cardiobacterium hominis; Eikenella corrodens; Kingella kingae (HACEK group, all gram negative bacilli).

parts.text: What are the 5 most common gram (-) causes of infective endocarditis?

questions.model_answer: The five most common gram-negative causes of infective endocarditis: the HACEK group (Haemophilus, Aggregatibacter [formerly Actinobacillus], Cardiobacterium, Eikenella, Kingella species), Escherichia coli, Pseudomonas aeruginosa, Klebsiella species, and Serratia marcescens (the last four comprising the most common non-HACEK gram-negative bacilli causing IE).

parts.text: Culture negative endocarditis – what are the 5 most common gram negative causes of IE?

cohort_answer.text: Last year's answer (assuming native valve, HACEK 2%): Haemophilus spp.; Aggregatibacter actinomycetemcomitans; Cardiobacterium hominis; Eikinella corrodens; Kingella kingae. Non-HACEK GNB (2%): E coli; K pneumoniae. From IDSA/AHA guidelines: HACEK 5-10% of community acquired NVE in non-IVDU: Haemophilus species, Aggregatibacter species, Cardiobacterium hominis, Eikenella corrodens, and Kingella species. Probably go with HACEK as the group for most common GNB IE causes

cohort_answer.text: Consider LGV (Chlamydia trachomatis serovars L1, L2, L3). Request special testing for LGV from urine (+/- rectal, throat) +/- LN aspiration. Treatment: doxy or azithro x21 days
Cipro 500mg PO x1 OR Azithro 1g PO x1 OR Ceftriaxone 250mg IM x1 - but increased failures in HIV. Chancroid = genital ulcer disease due to Haemophilus ducreyi, a fastidious Gram-negative rod

parts.text: List 3 pathogens (genus and species) in which Doxycycline CAN be considered for treatment for genital ulcers.

questions.model_answer: Three genital ulcer pathogens for which doxycycline can be considered: (1) Treponema pallidum (syphilis - doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x14 days is an alternative to penicillin). (2) Chlamydia trachomatis (lymphogranuloma venereum - doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x14-21 days). (3) Klebsiella granulomatis (donovanosis/granuloma inguinale - doxycycline for a minimum of 3 weeks or until lesions heal).
